skill.name: python-executor
skill.description: Run Python 3.10 code through the inference.sh executor with preinstalled libraries for data, web, media, documents, and 3D processing.
skill.summary: Execute Python workloads remotely and return console output or generated files.
skill.author: 101-skills

security_audit.summary: The skill intentionally invokes the belt CLI, submits arbitrary Python to a third-party execution service, and demonstrates outbound HTTP requests. Most backtick detections are Markdown formatting, and the reconnaissance alert is unsupported, but remote execution, network access, and unpinned npx installation remain real risks.

remediation.issue: Python source and embedded data are submitted to a third-party execution service.
remediation.suggestion: Disclose the remote processing boundary and instruct users to remove secrets, credentials, and sensitive data before execution.

remediation.issue: Generated Python can make outbound network requests from the execution environment.
remediation.suggestion: Require explicit approval for network access and recommend domain allowlists, request timeouts, and response size limits.

remediation.issue: The installation guidance executes an unpinned package through npx.
remediation.suggestion: Pin the installer package to a reviewed version and provide checksum or provenance verification instructions.

content.user_title: Run Python Workloads in a Remote Sandbox
content.value_statement: Complex Python tasks often require libraries and an isolated runtime. This skill submits code to inference.sh and returns console output or generated files.
actual_capabilities: Runs Python 3.10 code through the infsh/python-executor application.
Processes and visualizes data with NumPy, Pandas, SciPy, Matplotlib, Seaborn, and Plotly.
Makes HTTP requests and parses web content with common Python libraries.
Creates image, video, audio, document, and 3D model files.
Returns files written to the outputs directory with captured console output.
limitations: Requires the belt CLI, an inference.sh account, and network access.
Uses a CPU-only remote environment without GPU machine learning libraries.
Supports non-interactive execution with a maximum documented timeout of 300 seconds.
Submitted code and embedded data are processed by a third-party service.

use_cases.title: Analyze Operational Data
use_cases.description: Clean a dataset, calculate summary metrics, and generate charts without preparing a local Python environment.

use_cases.title: Automate Web Research
use_cases.description: Request approved public pages, parse selected fields, and return a structured summary.

use_cases.title: Generate Technical Assets
use_cases.description: Create images, PDF reports, short videos, or 3D model exports from defined inputs.

prompt_templates.title: Run a Simple Calculation
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the Python executor to calculate [calculation]. Show the result and briefly explain the method.
prompt_templates.scenario: A beginner needs a verified numerical result.

prompt_templates.title: Summarize a Dataset
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze [dataset description] with Pandas. Report missing values, key statistics, and notable patterns. Do not include sensitive data.
prompt_templates.scenario: An analyst needs a concise data quality and trend review.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Downloadable Report
prompt_templates.prompt: Process [input data] and create a PDF report in the outputs directory. Include [sections] and charts for [metrics].
prompt_templates.scenario: A user needs a generated document and supporting visuals.

prompt_templates.title: Build a Controlled Research Pipeline
prompt_templates.prompt: Request only [approved domains], enforce timeouts and response limits, extract [fields], validate results, and save the final table to outputs.
prompt_templates.scenario: An advanced user needs a bounded network data workflow.

output_examples.input: Analyze monthly sales by region and create a chart.
output: Console summary: West had the highest total sales, followed by North.

output_examples.output: The execution completed successfully and returned gradient.png from the outputs directory.

output_examples.input: Inspect a 3D sphere model and report its size.
output_examples.output: The result reports vertex and face counts, bounding dimensions, and a returned sphere.stl file.

best_practices: Remove credentials and sensitive data before submitting code or inputs.
Set the shortest practical timeout and write required artifacts to the outputs directory.
Use approved domains, request timeouts, and response size limits for network tasks.
anti_patterns: Do not place API keys, tokens, passwords, or private records inside submitted code.
Do not scrape restricted sites or bypass access controls and usage policies.
Do not rely on interactive windows, GPU acceleration, or unlimited execution time.

faq.question: Does this skill run Python locally?
faq.answer: No. It uses the belt CLI to submit code to the inference.sh Python executor.

faq.question: Can it install additional packages?
faq.answer: The skill documents more than 100 pre-installed libraries but does not document runtime package installation.

faq.question: How are generated files returned?
faq.answer: Files written to the outputs directory are detected and included in the execution response.

faq.question: Can it access websites and APIs?
faq.answer: Yes. Included HTTP libraries can make network requests, subject to service controls and target policies.

faq.question: Is sensitive data safe to submit?
faq.answer: Treat execution as third-party processing. Remove secrets and confidential data unless service terms and organizational policies permit submission.
